answer: Because the bridge index resolves every citation against the trellis checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the river audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 221 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 221 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 26 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
